1.headline: Big Climate Meeting Ends With No Deal
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
A big world meeting about the climate ended with no deal.

The meeting was in Turkey. Many countries came to talk about the Earth. They want to stop the planet from getting too hot. The talks went two days longer than planned. It was the longest meeting of its kind. But in the end, there was no main deal.

Why? The countries did not agree about oil, gas and coal. When we burn them, the Earth gets hotter. Europe wanted the deal to talk about using less oil and gas. Some oil countries did not want these words.
The head of the United Nations was very sad about it. The next meeting will be in Ethiopia.
Again, the climate meeting in Turkey ended with no deal.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
기후에 관한 큰 세계 회의가 합의 없이 끝났습니다.
회의는 튀르키예에서 열렸습니다. 많은 나라가 지구에 대해 이야기하려고 모였습니다. 이들은 지구가 너무 뜨거워지는 것을 막고 싶어 합니다. 회의는 계획보다 이틀 더 길어졌습니다. 이런 회의 가운데 가장 긴 회의였습니다. 하지만 결국 핵심 합의는 나오지 않았습니다.
왜일까요? 나라들이 석유, 가스, 석탄에 대해 의견이 맞지 않았습니다. 이것들을 태우면 지구가 더 뜨거워집니다. 유럽은 합의문에 석유와 가스를 덜 쓰자는 내용이 들어가길 원했습니다. 일부 산유국은 이런 표현을 원하지 않았습니다.
유엔 사무총장은 이에 대해 매우 실망했습니다. 다음 회의는 에티오피아에서 열립니다.
다시 말해, 튀르키예에서 열린 기후 회의가 합의 없이 끝났습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: UN Climate Talks in Turkey End Without a Deal
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
The longest United Nations climate meeting ever has ended with no main deal.

According to news reports, the meeting is called COP31. It took place in Antalya, Turkey. Countries planned to finish on November 20th. But they kept talking for about two more days. On Sunday, the meeting ended without its main agreement.

The biggest problem was fossil fuels. Fossil fuels are coal, oil and gas. Burning them makes the planet warmer. The European Union wanted the final paper to talk about moving away from them. Small island countries like the Marshall Islands agreed. But reports say Saudi Arabia and Russia wanted to keep those words out.
The head of the United Nations, Antonio Guterres, said he was deeply disappointed. He said the science is very clear, even if countries do not agree.

Why does this matter? Many countries are already facing stronger storms and rising seas. Poor countries also want more money to deal with these problems. Without a deal, it is harder to know what will happen next. The next meeting will be in Ethiopia.
To sum up, the UN climate talks in Turkey ended with no main deal because countries could not agree on fossil fuels.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
역대 가장 길었던 유엔 기후 회의가 핵심 합의 없이 끝났습니다.
보도에 따르면 이 회의의 이름은 COP31입니다. 회의는 튀르키예 안탈리아에서 열렸습니다. 각국은 11월 20일에 끝낼 계획이었습니다. 하지만 이틀 정도 더 논의를 이어 갔습니다. 일요일에 회의는 핵심 합의 없이 끝났습니다.
가장 큰 문제는 화석 연료였습니다. 화석 연료는 석탄, 석유, 가스를 말합니다. 이것들을 태우면 지구가 더 따뜻해집니다. 유럽연합은 최종 문서에 화석 연료에서 벗어나자는 내용을 담기를 원했습니다. 마셜 제도 같은 작은 섬나라들도 같은 생각이었습니다. 하지만 보도에 따르면 사우디아라비아와 러시아는 그런 표현을 빼기를 원했습니다.
안토니우 구테흐스 유엔 사무총장은 깊이 실망했다고 말했습니다. 그는 나라들이 합의하지 못하더라도 과학은 매우 분명하다고 말했습니다.
이것이 왜 중요할까요? 많은 나라가 이미 더 강한 폭풍과 높아지는 바다를 겪고 있습니다. 가난한 나라들은 이런 문제에 대응할 돈도 더 많이 원합니다. 합의가 없으면 앞으로 무슨 일이 일어날지 알기 더 어렵습니다. 다음 회의는 에티오피아에서 열립니다.
정리하면, 튀르키예에서 열린 유엔 기후 회의는 나라들이 화석 연료에 합의하지 못해 핵심 합의 없이 끝났습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

3.headline: UN Climate Talks End Without a Main Deal Over Fossil Fuels
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
The longest United Nations climate meeting in history has ended, and countries could not agree on its main deal.

According to news reports, the talks, called COP31, took place in Antalya, Turkey. They were planned to finish on November 20th. But the countries kept talking for about two more days. On Sunday, the meeting closed without its main agreement. Turkey and Australia led the talks together.

The biggest fight was about fossil fuels. Fossil fuels are coal, oil and gas. When we burn them, they warm the planet. The European Union, Panama and the Marshall Islands said the final text must talk about moving away from fossil fuels. But reports say Saudi Arabia and Russia pushed to keep those words out. The draft also supported carbon capture. Carbon capture means catching pollution before it goes into the air. Some critics say this could become an excuse to keep using oil and gas.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was deeply disappointed. He said countries may not agree in the meeting room, but the science is not unclear at all.

Why does this matter? In 2023, countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels. To transition means to slowly change from one thing to another. Without a new deal, it is harder to see how countries will keep that promise. Poor countries and small island nations also wanted more money to deal with storms and rising seas. The next meeting, COP32, will be in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
To sum up, the UN climate talks in Turkey ended without a main deal, because countries could not agree on fossil fuels.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
역사상 가장 길었던 유엔 기후 회의가 끝났지만, 각국은 핵심 합의에 이르지 못했습니다.
보도에 따르면 COP31이라는 이 회의는 튀르키예 안탈리아에서 열렸습니다. 원래 11월 20일에 끝날 예정이었습니다. 하지만 각국은 이틀 정도 더 논의를 이어 갔습니다. 일요일에 회의는 핵심 합의 없이 막을 내렸습니다. 튀르키예와 호주가 함께 회의를 이끌었습니다.

가장 큰 다툼은 화석 연료를 둘러싼 것이었습니다. 화석 연료는 석탄, 석유, 가스를 말합니다. 이것들을 태우면 지구가 따뜻해집니다. 유럽연합과 파나마, 마셜 제도는 최종 문서에 화석 연료에서 벗어나자는 내용이 꼭 들어가야 한다고 말했습니다. 하지만 보도에 따르면 사우디아라비아와 러시아는 그런 표현을 빼자고 밀어붙였습니다. 초안은 탄소 포집도 지지했습니다. 탄소 포집은 오염 물질이 공기 중으로 나가기 전에 붙잡는 것을 말합니다. 일부 비판자들은 이것이 석유와 가스를 계속 쓰는 핑계가 될 수 있다고 말합니다.
안토니우 구테흐스 유엔 사무총장은 깊이 실망했다고 말했습니다. 그는 회의장에서는 각국이 합의하지 못할 수 있어도, 과학은 전혀 불분명하지 않다고 말했습니다.

이것이 왜 중요할까요? 2023년에 각국은 화석 연료에서 벗어나는 전환에 합의했습니다. 전환이란 한 가지에서 다른 것으로 천천히 바꿔 가는 것을 뜻합니다. 새 합의가 없으면 각국이 그 약속을 어떻게 지킬지 알기 더 어렵습니다. 가난한 나라와 작은 섬나라들은 폭풍과 해수면 상승에 대처할 돈도 더 많이 원했습니다. 다음 회의인 COP32는 에티오피아 아디스아바바에서 열립니다.
정리하면, 튀르키예에서 열린 유엔 기후 회의는 각국이 화석 연료에 합의하지 못해 핵심 합의 없이 끝났습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

4.headline: COP31 Collapses Without a Deal After Fossil Fuel Dispute
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
After running nearly two days past its deadline, the longest UN climate summit on record has ended without its main agreement.

According to news reports, the COP31 talks in the Turkish city of Antalya were scheduled to wrap up on November 20th. Negotiators kept working through the weekend, but on Sunday the summit's central decision was rejected. Turkey hosted the conference and shared the presidency with Australia.

The deal fell apart over fossil fuels. The European Union, along with countries such as Panama and the Marshall Islands, refused to accept a final text that made no clear reference to moving away from coal, oil and gas. Reports say Saudi Arabia and Russia were influential in keeping that language out. The draft also backed carbon capture and storage, a technology that traps emissions before they reach the atmosphere. Critics argue it could be used to justify continued fossil fuel use, while Saudi Arabia defended the references.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was deeply disappointed. He noted that while there may be no consensus in the negotiating room, there is no ambiguity in the science, which points to fossil fuels as the main driver of global warming.

The breakdown matters because, in 2023, nearly every country agreed to transition away from fossil fuels. Without a new decision, there is no fresh plan showing how that pledge will be met. Developing countries and climate-vulnerable island states had also pressed for stronger commitments on financial support, saying the proposals fell short. Attention now turns to COP32, which will be held in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
To sum up, the COP31 climate summit in Turkey ended without a main deal after countries split over whether to mention fossil fuels, leaving the global plan to cut emissions uncertain.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.
마감 시한을 이틀 가까이 넘긴 끝에, 기록상 가장 긴 유엔 기후 정상회의가 핵심 합의 없이 끝났습니다.
보도에 따르면 튀르키예 도시 안탈리아에서 열린 COP31 회의는 11월 20일에 마무리될 예정이었습니다. 협상가들은 주말 내내 논의를 이어 갔지만, 일요일에 회의의 핵심 결정문이 거부되었습니다. 튀르키예가 회의를 주최했고 호주와 의장직을 함께 맡았습니다.

합의는 화석 연료 문제로 무산되었습니다. 유럽연합은 파나마, 마셜 제도 같은 나라들과 함께, 석탄·석유·가스에서 벗어나는 것에 대한 분명한 언급이 없는 최종 문서를 받아들이지 않았습니다. 보도에 따르면 사우디아라비아와 러시아가 그런 표현을 빼는 데 큰 영향력을 행사했습니다. 초안은 또한 배출가스가 대기에 닿기 전에 붙잡는 기술인 탄소 포집·저장을 지지했습니다. 비판자들은 이것이 화석 연료를 계속 쓰는 것을 정당화하는 데 이용될 수 있다고 주장했고, 사우디아라비아는 해당 내용을 옹호했습니다.
안토니우 구테흐스 유엔 사무총장은 깊이 실망했다고 말했습니다. 그는 협상장에서는 합의가 없을 수 있지만 과학에는 모호함이 없으며, 과학은 화석 연료를 지구 온난화의 주된 원인으로 지목한다고 강조했습니다.

이번 결렬이 중요한 이유는 2023년에 거의 모든 나라가 화석 연료에서 벗어나는 전환에 합의했기 때문입니다. 새 결정이 없으면 그 약속을 어떻게 지킬지 보여 주는 새로운 계획도 없습니다. 개발도상국과 기후 위기에 취약한 섬나라들은 재정 지원에 대한 더 강한 약속도 요구하며, 제안이 부족하다고 말했습니다. 이제 관심은 에티오피아 아디스아바바에서 열릴 COP32로 옮겨 갑니다.
정리하면, 튀르키예에서 열린 COP31 기후 정상회의는 화석 연료 언급 여부를 놓고 각국이 갈라서면서 핵심 합의 없이 끝났고, 배출 감축을 위한 세계적 계획은 불확실해졌습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

5.headline: COP31 Ends in Deadlock as Fossil Fuel Language Splits Nations
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Nearly two days into overtime, the longest UN climate summit ever held has unravelled, leaving negotiators with no headline agreement to show for their efforts.

According to news reports, the COP31 talks in Antalya, on Turkey's Mediterranean coast, were due to conclude on November 20th. Delegates pressed on through the weekend in a last-ditch bid to bridge their differences, but on Sunday the summit's central cover decision was rejected. Turkey hosted the gathering and shared the presidency with Australia, an unusual arrangement that had itself drawn attention.

The sticking point was fossil fuels. The European Union, joined by countries including Panama and the Marshall Islands, refused to sign off on a text that omitted any explicit reference to transitioning away from coal, oil and gas. Reports indicate that Saudi Arabia and Russia were instrumental in keeping that wording out. The draft also endorsed carbon capture and storage, a technology that traps emissions before they reach the atmosphere. Detractors warn it could serve as a pretext for prolonging fossil fuel use, while Saudi Arabia, speaking for the Arab group, defended those references.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres declared himself deeply disappointed. There may be no consensus in the negotiating room, he observed, but there is no ambiguity in the science, which identifies fossil fuels as the primary driver of global warming.

The stakes are considerable. In 2023, nearly every nation signed up to a pledge to transition away from fossil fuels, and this summit was widely seen as a test of whether that promise would be translated into concrete action. Instead, it ended with no fresh roadmap. Developing countries and climate-vulnerable island states, which bear the brunt of intensifying storms and rising seas, had also lobbied for firmer commitments on finance, arguing that the proposals on the table fell well short. All eyes now turn to COP32 in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
To sum up, COP31 in Turkey broke down without a main deal after nations clashed over whether to name fossil fuels, casting fresh doubt on the world's collective plan to curb emissions.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스에 오신 것을 환영합니다.
연장전에 들어간 지 이틀 가까이 지나, 역대 가장 길었던 유엔 기후 정상회의가 결국 무너졌고, 협상가들은 그간의 노력에도 내세울 핵심 합의를 얻지 못했습니다.
보도에 따르면 튀르키예 지중해 연안의 안탈리아에서 열린 COP31 회의는 11월 20일에 마칠 예정이었습니다. 대표단은 이견을 좁히려는 마지막 시도로 주말까지 강행했지만, 일요일에 회의의 핵심 총괄 결정문이 거부되었습니다. 튀르키예가 회의를 주최했고 호주와 의장직을 나눠 맡았는데, 이 이례적인 방식 자체도 관심을 모았습니다.

걸림돌은 화석 연료였습니다. 유럽연합은 파나마와 마셜 제도 등과 함께, 석탄·석유·가스로부터의 전환에 대한 명시적 언급이 빠진 문서를 승인하지 않았습니다. 보도에 따르면 사우디아라비아와 러시아가 그 문구를 빼는 데 결정적인 역할을 했습니다. 초안은 또 배출가스가 대기에 닿기 전에 가두는 기술인 탄소 포집·저장을 지지했습니다. 반대론자들은 이것이 화석 연료 사용을 연장하는 구실이 될 수 있다고 경고했고, 아랍 그룹을 대표해 발언한 사우디아라비아는 해당 내용을 옹호했습니다.
안토니우 구테흐스 유엔 사무총장은 깊이 실망했다고 밝혔습니다. 그는 협상장에는 합의가 없을지 몰라도 과학에는 모호함이 없으며, 과학은 화석 연료를 지구 온난화의 주된 원인으로 지목한다고 말했습니다.

걸린 것이 큽니다. 2023년 거의 모든 나라가 화석 연료에서 벗어나는 전환을 약속했고, 이번 회의는 그 약속이 구체적인 행동으로 이어질지를 가늠하는 시험대로 널리 여겨졌습니다. 그러나 회의는 새로운 로드맵 없이 끝났습니다. 거세지는 폭풍과 해수면 상승의 피해를 가장 크게 입는 개발도상국과 기후 취약 섬나라들은 재원에 대한 더 확고한 약속도 요구하며, 논의 중인 제안이 크게 부족하다고 주장했습니다. 이제 모든 시선은 에티오피아 아디스아바바에서 열릴 COP32로 향합니다.
정리하면, 튀르키예에서 열린 COP31은 화석 연료를 명시할지를 두고 각국이 충돌하면서 핵심 합의 없이 결렬되었고, 배출을 억제하려는 세계 공동의 계획에 다시 의문이 제기되었습니다.
들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

1.headline: A Very Old Library in Rome Opens Again
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Would you like to visit a library from almost two thousand years ago?
Now you can, in Rome, Italy. The library was built by the Romans long ago. It had books in Greek. People found it in 1932. But then it was closed for almost one hundred years.
Workers fixed it in about one year. The work cost one point seven five million euros. Visitors can now see old stone, broken columns and video on the walls.
Did you know? Old books were not like our books. They were long rolls of paper.
Visitors go in small groups of twenty. For now, it is open on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays.
Again, a very old library in Rome is open to visitors.
Thank you for listening.
tr: 좋은 아침입니다. 영어로 듣는 아침 뉴스입니다.
거의 2천 년 전의 도서관에 가 보고 싶으신가요?

2.headline: Ancient Library in Rome Opens to Visitors
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
A library that was hidden for almost one hundred years is now open in Rome.

According to news reports, it is called the Ulpia Library. It was part of the forum of Emperor Trajan. A forum was a big public square with buildings around it. The forum was built in the year 112. The library had scrolls in Greek.
People found the library in 1932, during road work. But it was in ruins. Later, it was covered with concrete and used as a storage room.

Workers started fixing it in 2025. The project took about a year and cost one point seven five million euros. The money came from the European Union. Now visitors can see marble, broken columns and pieces of statues. Videos on the walls tell the story of the library.
Did you know? Ancient books were scrolls, long rolls of paper you open slowly.
An official in Rome said it was one of the most important libraries of the ancient world. Visitors go in groups of twenty, on weekends for now.
To sum up, an ancient library in Rome is open to the public after a long time.
Thank you for listening.

정리하면, 로마의 고대 도서관이 오랜 시간 끝에 일반에 공개되었습니다.

3.headline: Rome's Long-Buried Ulpia Library Opens to the Public
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
For almost a century, one of the great libraries of ancient Rome was used as a storage room. Now, anyone can walk inside.

According to news reports, the Ulpia Library has opened to visitors after a restoration. A restoration means repairing something old so it looks more like it once did. The library is in the Forum of Trajan, a large public square built for the Roman emperor Trajan in the year 112. It stands next to the famous Trajan's Column.

The library had two buildings. Experts say one held scrolls in Greek, and the other held scrolls in Latin. Did you know? Ancient books were not pages but long rolls, which readers opened slowly as they read.
The Greek building was found in 1932, during work on a new road. But it was badly damaged. Later, it was covered with concrete and used to store pieces from the forum.

Work started in 2025 and took about a year. It cost one point seven five million euros, paid for with European Union recovery funds after the pandemic. Visitors can now see marble decorations, broken columns and pieces of statues. Videos shown on the walls tell the library's story.

Rome's top heritage official said it was one of the most important libraries of the ancient world, after the famous libraries of Alexandria and Pergamon. For now, small groups of twenty can visit on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays. The Latin building is still under an old church, with no plans to dig it up.
To sum up, a long-hidden ancient library in Rome is now open, so visitors can see where Romans once read their scrolls.
Thank you for listening.

4.headline: Ancient Ulpia Library Reopens in Rome After Nearly a Century
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Imagine a library that held some of the most valuable texts of the Roman world, then spent decades serving as a storage room. That library has just reopened.

According to news reports, the Ulpia Library, part of the Forum of Trajan in central Rome, is now open to the public following a restoration. The forum, built in 112 for the emperor Trajan, sits beside Trajan's Column, one of the city's best-known monuments.

Ancient sources describe the library as two buildings facing each other. Archaeologists believe one housed Greek-language scrolls and the other Latin ones. The niches in the walls were designed to hold the cabinets where those scrolls were kept.

The Greek building was uncovered in 1932, when Mussolini's government cleared land to build a major road through the area. By then it lay in ruins. It was later sealed under concrete and used as a storeroom for fragments from the forum, and it remained off limits for almost a century.

The restoration began in 2025, lasted about a year and cost one point seven five million euros, funded by the European Union's pandemic recovery program. A new permanent exhibition displays remains of the marble decoration, broken Corinthian columns and sculpture fragments, while video projections on the walls trace the library's history and its rediscovery.

Rome's superintendent for cultural heritage, Claudio Parisi Presicce, told reporters the library ranked among the most important of antiquity, behind only those of Alexandria and Pergamon. Visits are initially limited to Fridays through Sundays, in groups of twenty. The Latin building, meanwhile, remains buried beneath an 18th-century church, and there are no plans to excavate it.
To sum up, Rome's Ulpia Library, hidden for nearly a hundred years, has reopened with a new exhibition that brings an ancient reading room back to life.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Rome Unveils the Restored Ulpia Library, Lost to View for a Century
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Once a treasure house of Greek and Latin learning, then a concrete-sealed storeroom, one of the ancient world's great libraries has finally been returned to the public gaze.

According to news reports, the Ulpia Library, part of the Forum of Trajan in the heart of Rome, has reopened following an extensive restoration. The forum, completed in 112 for the emperor Trajan, sits in the shadow of Trajan's Column, among the most celebrated monuments of the imperial capital.

Ancient texts describe the library as a pair of two-story buildings facing each other across a courtyard. Archaeologists believe the western one housed Greek-language scrolls and its counterpart Latin ones, with niches in the walls designed to accommodate the cabinets that held them.

The Greek building came to light in 1932, when Mussolini's regime bulldozed swathes of the area to make way for a grand thoroughfare. By then it was little more than rubble. It was subsequently encased in concrete and pressed into service as a depot for architectural fragments, and for the best part of a century it was effectively off limits.

Work got underway in 2025 and took roughly a year, at a cost of one point seven five million euros drawn from the European Union's pandemic recovery funds, which have bankrolled a raft of restoration projects across the city. A new permanent exhibition showcases surviving marble decoration, toppled Corinthian columns and sculptural fragments, while immersive video mapping on the walls recounts the library's history and its rediscovery.

Claudio Parisi Presicce, Rome's superintendent for cultural heritage, told reporters that the library ranked among the foremost of antiquity, eclipsed only by those of Alexandria and Pergamon. Admission is initially restricted to weekends, from Friday to Sunday, in timed groups of twenty. The Latin building, by contrast, still lies entombed beneath an 18th-century church, and there are no plans to unearth it.
To sum up, after almost a hundred years out of sight, Rome's Ulpia Library has reopened, offering visitors a rare glimpse of where the Romans once consulted their scrolls.
Thank you for listening.

1.headline: Rich and Poor in North Korea
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
In North Korea, some leaders carry very expensive bags.

The Korea Herald wrote about this. In photos, top people in North Korea have bags from famous fashion brands. Kim Jong Un wore a watch worth about fourteen thousand dollars. A big boat was also seen near the sea. It had a pool and a water slide.
But life is hard for many people. The price of rice went up about seven times since early 2024. Many families buy food at local markets.
North Korea's economy grew in the last three years. Experts say help from Russia is one reason. But they say this may not last.
Again, some leaders in North Korea are rich, but many people have a hard life.
Thank you for listening.

들어 주셔서 감사합니다.

2.headline: Luxury for a Few, Hard Times for Many in North Korea
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
Designer bags and a giant boat with a water slide. This is how some people live in North Korea.

According to a report in the Korea Herald, the gap between rich and poor in North Korea is growing. In photos, top officials carry bags from famous brands like Dior. Kim Jong Un wore a Swiss watch reportedly worth about fourteen thousand dollars. The BBC also showed satellite pictures of a large yacht, or luxury boat, with a pool and a water slide.
This is surprising because United Nations rules ban selling luxury goods to North Korea.

Life is very different for ordinary people. A researcher in Seoul found that the price of rice rose about seven times since early 2024. Fuel prices also went up a lot. Many families depend on local markets to get food.

The Bank of Korea says North Korea's economy grew more than three percent for three years in a row. Experts link this to North Korea's close ties with Russia. But they warn the good times may not last.
To sum up, North Korea's leaders enjoy luxury goods while many ordinary people struggle with high prices.
Thank you for listening.

3.headline: North Korea's Elite Show Off Luxury as Ordinary People Face Rising Prices
p: Good morning. This is your morning news in English.
A yacht with a swimming pool and a water slide, floating off the coast of North Korea. Who is it for?

According to a report in the Korea Herald, the gap between North Korea's elite and its ordinary people is growing wider. The elite are the small group of people at the top with the most power and money.

The report points to photos of top officials. Some carried bags from luxury brands such as Dior and Saint Laurent. Kim Jong Un wore a Swiss watch reportedly worth about fourteen thousand dollars. Satellite images shown by the BBC revealed a yacht about eighty meters long near the city of Wonsan. Reports say a department store in Pyongyang, the capital, sells luxury brands too. This stands out because United Nations sanctions ban selling luxury goods to North Korea. Sanctions are rules that punish a country by limiting trade.

Life looks very different for most people. A researcher at a South Korean government-funded institute found that the price of rice rose by about six hundred percent from early 2024 to this year. That means rice costs about seven times more. Fuel prices also jumped. Many families depend on local markets, called jangmadang, to survive.

Why is this happening? The Bank of Korea estimates that North Korea's economy grew more than three percent for three years in a row. Experts link this growth to North Korea's close ties with Russia, including military support. But the researcher called it a temporary boom for the government, not for the people. He warned it could end quickly if Russia stops buying.
To sum up, North Korea's leaders are enjoying luxury goods, while ordinary people struggle with sharply rising prices.
Thank you for listening.

코리아헤럴드 보도에 따르면 북한 엘리트층과 보통 주민 사이의 격차가 더 커지고 있습니다. 엘리트층이란 가장 많은 권력과 돈을 가진 최상위의 소수 집단을 말합니다.

대부분의 사람들에게 삶은 매우 다르게 보입니다. 한국의 한 정부 출연 연구소 연구원은 쌀값이 2024년 초부터 올해까지 약 600% 올랐다는 것을 알아냈습니다. 쌀값이 약 7배가 되었다는 뜻입니다. 연료 가격도 급등했습니다. 많은 가정이 살아가기 위해 장마당이라고 불리는 지역 시장에 의존합니다.
왜 이런 일이 일어날까요? 한국은행은 북한 경제가 3년 연속 3% 넘게 성장한 것으로 추정합니다. 전문가들은 이 성장을 군사 지원을 포함한 북한과 러시아의 긴밀한 관계와 연결 짓습니다. 하지만 그 연구원은 이것이 주민이 아닌 정권을 위한 일시적 호황이라고 말했습니다. 그는 러시아가 구매를 멈추면 이것이 빠르게 끝날 수 있다고 경고했습니다.

4.headline: Report Highlights a Widening Divide Between North Korea's Elite and Its People
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.
Designer handbags, a Swiss watch and an eighty-meter yacht complete with a water slide are not what most people picture when they think of North Korea.
According to a report published by the Korea Herald, the country's ruling elite are enjoying a lifestyle that stands in sharp contrast to the hardships faced by ordinary citizens.

The report cites photographs of senior officials carrying bags from luxury labels such as Dior and Saint Laurent, and of Kim Jong Un wearing a Swiss watch reportedly valued at around fourteen thousand dollars. Satellite imagery published by the BBC showed a large yacht moored off the eastern city of Wonsan for several months. In Pyongyang, a major department store is reported to stock high-end international brands. All of this comes despite United Nations sanctions that prohibit the sale of luxury goods to North Korea.

For ordinary households, the picture is very different. A researcher at a South Korean state-funded think tank found that the price of rice climbed roughly six hundred percent between early 2024 and the third quarter of this year, with fuel prices rising at a similar pace. Many families rely on informal markets, known as jangmadang, to get by.

The contrast comes as North Korea's economy expands. The Bank of Korea estimates growth topped three percent for a third straight year in 2025, a trend analysts attribute largely to deepening cooperation with Russia, including military support. However, the researcher described the gains as a temporary windfall for the regime's finances rather than broad prosperity, and warned they could reverse sharply if Russian demand dries up.
To sum up, a new report suggests North Korea's elite are benefiting from recent economic growth, while ordinary people grapple with soaring prices for basic goods.
Thank you for listening.

5.headline: Opulence at the Top, Austerity Below: North Korea's Deepening Economic Divide
p: Good morning, and welcome to your morning news in English.

Designer handbags, a pricey Swiss timepiece and an eighty-meter yacht boasting its own water slide hardly square with the image of an isolated, sanctions-hit state, yet that is precisely the lifestyle North Korea's ruling class appears to enjoy.
According to a report in the Korea Herald, the gulf between the country's privileged elite and its ordinary citizens is widening, even as the economy continues to expand.

The report draws on photographs of senior officials sporting bags from luxury houses such as Dior and Saint Laurent, and of Kim Jong Un wearing a Swiss watch reportedly worth some fourteen thousand dollars. Satellite imagery published by the BBC showed a sizeable yacht anchored off the eastern port city of Wonsan for months on end, while a flagship department store in Pyongyang is said to carry high-end Western labels. All of this flies in the face of United Nations sanctions that expressly bar the supply of luxury goods to the North, though their reach ultimately hinges on enforcement.

Beyond the capital's showrooms, the reality is starkly different. A researcher at a state-funded South Korean think tank calculated that rice prices soared by roughly six hundred percent between early 2024 and the third quarter of this year, with fuel costs spiralling at a comparable rate. Many households, meanwhile, are left to fend for themselves through informal markets, known as jangmadang, where prices are set by supply and demand.

The paradox is underpinned by a growth spurt. The Bank of Korea estimates the North's economy expanded by more than three percent for a third consecutive year in 2025, a surge analysts largely credit to burgeoning ties with Moscow, including military assistance. Yet the researcher characterized the upswing as predatory growth, a fleeting boon to the regime's coffers rather than a tide that lifts all boats, and cautioned that it could unravel abruptly should Russian demand evaporate.
To sum up, a new report paints a picture of North Korea's elite reaping the rewards of recent growth, while ordinary people bear the burden of runaway prices for everyday necessities.
Thank you for listening.
